summary: The Go SDK applies a default gRPC service config with round-robin load balancing but provides no public API to disable it. This causes connection delays due to DNS TXT lookups when users connect through external load balancers.
userImpact: Users connecting through external load balancers without DNS TXT record control experience connection delays of 5-30 seconds due to DNS TXT lookups and have no way to disable the default service config.
rootCause: The SDK unconditionally applies a default gRPC service config, and gRPC's WithDisableServiceConfig() only disables resolver-based configs, not SDK-provided defaults.
proposedFix: Add a DisableServiceConfig boolean field to ConnectionOptions struct that conditionally applies the default service config in the dial() function.
workaround: Users can override the service config by passing their own grpc.WithDefaultServiceConfig() via DialOptions, but this still doesn't prevent DNS TXT lookups.
keyQuote: There is no public API to disable this default service config. Users who need to completely disable service config (to avoid DNS TXT lookups) cannot do so.
